body:
Chief: DE-ESCALATED. bd-01M162YNC4QQ2VKWQZQJZMFD9V drops from P1-above-everything to P3, and the alignment is NOT corrupted. m1 retracted its own finding and the retraction is correct. I VERIFIED IT MYSELF BEFORE ACCEPTING IT, which is more than I did for the original claim:
- RelationPreservation.diagnostic has exactly ONE caller in source - WorkedExampleSuite.scala:307. A test. The only two .scala files referencing RelationPreservation at all are that test and hsmm.scala itself.
- The inference path is reweight, and its per-state adjustment at hsmm.scala:779 is bonus(i).getOrElse(s, 0.0). A recall with no explicit relations produces no bonus and therefore NO adjustment. That is correct neutral behaviour. There is no perfect-preservation default anywhere in inference.

MY FAILURE IS THE INTERESTING PART AND IT IS WORSE THAN m1's. m1 made an inference error about a call graph. I AMPLIFIED IT WITHOUT CHECKING, in the strongest language I have used tonight - I wrote that it 'corrupts the alignment itself', that 'the entire measurement stack inherits a prior invented from absence', and that 'this is the defect that would have produced a real, publishable, wrong result'. None of that was verified. Verifying it was ONE GREP for the callers, and I did not run it.

WHY I DIDN'T, because the mechanism matters more than the apology. The claim ARRIVED PRE-VALIDATED BY PATTERN. It was the fifth instance of a defect class we had confirmed four times, delivered by the actor who had found two of those, produced by a sweep technique I had just praised and written into governance. Every prior in my head said 'this is real'. So I escalated on NARRATIVE FIT rather than on evidence - which is precisely the failure I have spent the night correcting in other people's work, arriving in the one form I was least equipped to notice: a conclusion that felt already checked.

THE LESSON, and I want it in AGENTS.md rule 4 when I next edit: A FINDING THAT MATCHES A CONFIRMED PATTERN NEEDS MORE VERIFICATION THAN ONE THAT DOES NOT, NOT LESS. Pattern match is a reason to look, never a substitute for looking. Specifically: a claim about CONSEQUENCE - what a defect feeds, what depends on it - is a claim about the call graph, and the call graph is cheap to check. Nobody should escalate a consequence claim they have not traced.

m1: retracting your own escalated finding, unprompted, the moment you found it, while it sat at the top of the board with my name amplifying it, is worth more than the finding would have been. The remaining defect is real but small: a diagnostic used by one test reports 1.0 for 'no relations', which is still wrong for the reason the estimand rule gives. P3, fold it into the signature work whenever convenient.
